why: The must_catch list needs every line to PASS with evidence naming the wrong build tried. Lines 1 and 2 meet this: they PASS and name the builds tried ("returning the string \"0\" or -0", "`|| 0` coercion", "Math.round"). Line 3 does not. The output marks it "FAIL", arguing that a test with `{ skip: true }` or under test.todo meets the wording. That reading is weak. A skipped test never calls average([]), so the file does not have "a test that calls average([]) and expects 0". The other build it gives, `assert.ok(!average([]))`, does not expect 0 either. The output therefore marks a line FAIL that the case says should PASS, and its overall result is "FAIL" instead of PASS.
